comparator.sourceNotes: The current 2026–27 Leiden Study Guide study BA-JAP and its public product API identify 60 EC in each year. The chosen coherent pathway selects the Leiden 15-EC second-year route (Modern Japanese 2c, 10 EC, and a second shared East Asian course, 5 EC), rather than the Japan study-abroad route; one permitted option in each seminar and restricted-choice group; the BA Thesis 10 EC plus Graduation Seminar 5 EC rather than other graduation projects; and the full 30 EC genuine third-year elective space, split into two 15-EC components. The 0-EC mentorship and non-curricular JLPT preparation are excluded. The adopted OER confirms no formal graduation tracks and the 2026–27 language progression. Course EC were checked against the public 2026–27 module entries; the study grouping and selected options account for exactly 180 EC. Instruction metadata distinguish the formal Dutch programme classification from actual required courses: Japan in the 21st Century, Arts and Material Culture of Japan, Introduction to Modern Japanese History, and Power, Development and Conflict in Asia explicitly teach in English. Normalized NLD + ENG therefore records documented instruction; it does not mean that every course is English-taught. Japanese language learning alone does not establish Japanese-medium instruction. The fixed-queue UCR reassessment on 2026-10-16 preserves this settled 180-EC pathway and neutral Leiden option. The current programme page and adopted 2026–27 OER were rechecked: HUM/SOSCI remain disciplinary choice clusters rather than graduation tracks; the OER explicitly permits Modern Japanese 2c and records Japanese-source competence. The settled component reconstruction is preserved; the recheck concerns the academic identity and the material neutral-pathway rule rather than routine first-stage reconstruction.

exception.reason: Leiden combines progressive Japanese-language study with sustained investigation of Japanese history, society, arts and international relations and Japanese-source research. UCR can supply several associated disciplinary methods, but the current catalogue cannot sustain a complete related-fields response to this specifically Japan-centred evidence. This is not a requirement to reproduce the degree: history/society/international-relations and cultural/media approaches were tested separately as related alternatives. In each case the directly useful methods do not establish 23 substantive non-PPD course contributions; completing the programme requires unrelated regional specialisms, communication-production courses or additional imagined interests. The seven generator-eligible interests all explicitly concern Japan, and none establishes a separate general Western, American, African or Mediterranean studies direction. A Sony Walkman example in Media Archaeology does not establish a Japanese-culture sequence. No complete coherent 24-course programme is published.
exception.curriculumContext: The official 2026–27 study BA-JAP identifies 60 EC of first-year compulsory units, a 20-EC second-year compulsory group with 40 EC of restricted choices, and a 60-EC third year comprising 15 EC of restricted specialist study, one 15-EC graduation project pathway and 30 EC of actual elective space. The BA Thesis pathway is selected. The OER confirms Japanese-language progression and primary-source competence and describes HUM and SOSCI as clusters for course choices, not formal graduation tracks. The selected external components preserve all 180 EC without counting mutually exclusive Japan stay, alternative seminars or non-curricular language preparation.
exception.ucrCourseEvidence: Reassessed all 151 rows of current GitHub main data/reference/ucr_courses_enriched.xlsx, Git blob c2bcc3b63ec7831fd0f7b8ddfb32de1260521655, including profiles, descriptions, topics, methods, prerequisites and six planned cohort terms. (1) Japanese language/writing, row 13490 and support rows 13497–13500: no Japanese course, grammar/writing progression or Japanese-source training; HCBCOGN312 studies neurocognitive language processing, not Japanese. (2) History/society/international-relations, rows 13491,13493–13496 and support 13503–13510: GOSHIST111/211, GOSPOLI112/212/313 and GOSSOCI111/212/214/311 provide substantive methods for modernisation, empire, political institutions, international relations, conflict and social inquiry. They are useful related subjects, but do not teach a Japanese/East Asian regional sequence. GOSHIST312 specifically studies the 1809 Walcheren expedition; GOSHIST112/311 and MCCMEDI211/311 centre American histories and media, while GOSPOLI311 and GOSLAWJ312 centre Europe. Adding these simply to complete a Japan-linked response would replace its substantive question with other regions. Introductory/general economics or law can supply limited complements, but cannot justify an entire programme or a distinct additional direction from the evidenced Japanese interests. (3) Arts/material-culture with literary/media support, row 13492 and support 13501–13502: MCCLITR111/211/311/312, MCCMEDI111/112/312 and MCCHEAM312 offer literary interpretation, cross-cultural narrative, film adaptation, material-media analysis, documentary and museum approaches. MCCMEDI112 explicitly permits a Sony Walkman example, correcting the earlier absolute absence claim. This is an illustrative object rather than sustained Japanese material-culture study. Completing 24 courses would require Western art, Renaissance Mediterranean, Greek archaeology, African heritage, American media/race or generic communication-production additions without a specific contribution to the evidenced concept. Lack of language or professional qualification alone does not decide the outcome; inability to build a complete evidence-linked related programme does.
